title: Closed direct image is fully faithful at every coefficient stage
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type
$k$-schemes and let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient stages
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, with the categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the direct image
$i_*=Ri_*=Ri_!$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Then

$$
i_*:D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_c(X,\Lambda)
$$

is fully faithful. Consequently, at every stage at which $i_*$ has a right
adjoint $Ri^!$ on these categories (the exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]), the adjunction unit is an isomorphism

$$
Q\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ri^!i_*Q\qquad(Q\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)).
$$

At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ the right adjoint exists on the ambient categories and
this is [prop-sf-closed-immersion-unit].

proof.text: Keep the coefficient datum of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and $n\ge1$. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and itself, and its one-point spectrum is quasi-compact; applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structural maps makes $X,Z$ Noetherian. For every affine open $V\subset X$, the open subscheme $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], first to $V\subset X$ and then to $U\cap V\subset V$. Hence the complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact as a morphism, as required below. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc], $i$ is finite, separated and universally closed, hence proper (on affine charts a quotient algebra is generated by $1$ as a module and is of finite type). At finite level the compactification $Z\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Z\xrightarrow{i}X$ in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] computes $Ri_!=Ri_*$. For the higher stages, [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] uses the same compactification at every finite level: its integral tower is therefore exactly the direct-image tower, and its rationalization and common-stage functors are those of direct image as well. The symbol $i_*$ below denotes this derived direct image; the finite-level underived direct image computes it by step 3.

source.place: Finite-stage paragraph and the statement Ri_!=Ri_*; geometry and coefficient checks

proof.text: For $A=A_{E,n}$, [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] supplies $i^*\dashv Ri_{*,n}$ on the ordinary ambient pro-etale derived categories and an invertible counit $i^*Ri_{*,n}\to\mathrm{id}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-counit-iso-right-fully-faithful] to this very adjunction: $Ri_{*,n}$ is fully faithful on the entire ambient category. In particular its maps on Hom groups of any two bounded constructible objects are bijections.

source.place: Proof, finite-stage paragraph: invertible counit implies full faithfulness

proof.text: The quasi-compact-complement hypothesis of [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] holds by step 1, so finite-coefficient $i_*$ is exact. [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] realizes it termwise on derived categories. In particular a resolution $K\to I$ remains a quasi-isomorphism under $i_*$, so termwise $i_*K$ computes $Ri_{*,n}K$, and exactness gives $\mathcal H^r(Ri_{*,n}K)=i_*\mathcal H^r(K)$. To check constructibility directly, take the finite stratification of $Z$ for each constructible cohomology sheaf in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and adjoin the open stratum $U$. On a stratum lying in $Z$, restriction of $i_*G$ is restriction of $G$ by the module counit of [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful]; on $U$ it is zero by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image]. Thus the same finite locally constant modules, and the zero module on $U$, provide a constructible stratification on $X$. For a stratum $S=V\cap C$ in $Z$, write $V=Z\cap W$ with $W$ open in $X$; $C$ is closed in $X$ since $Z$ is closed, so $S=W\cap C$ is locally closed in $X$. It is constructible by the Noetherian clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset]; that clause also makes $U$ constructible. The cohomological interval is unchanged. Therefore the ambient fully faithful functor of step 2 restricts to the stated finite bounded constructible categories.

source.place: Proof, finite-stage paragraph: restriction to the full constructible subcategories; Stacks 09AA and 09BM (lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact)

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$ and $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$. The datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] agrees here with the completed integral coefficient sheaf in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: at $T=X,Z$ both are $R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$, and all finite levels are regarded as $R_T$-modules by the projection $R_T\to(A_n)_T$. The DVR and finite-quotient assertions in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] check the Noetherian, finite and additive-torsion assumptions of the adic datum; perfection of $A_n$ over $R$ follows from the two-term free resolution $0\to R\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}R\to A_n\to0$. Write $F$ for ordinary total derived ringed direct image over these completed sheaves, and $F_n=Ri_{*,n}$. The coefficient identification and the derived operations, including exactness and shift comparison, are [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For a finite-coefficient complex $M$, there is a canonical comparison $F\operatorname{Res}_nM\cong\operatorname{Res}_nF_nM$: both are derived direct image for the same composite ringed-topos morphism. Specifically, reducing the structural coefficient morphism before or after $i$ gives the same ring map, since its $n$-th projection commutes with inverse image. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to these two factorizations supplies the comparison; restriction is exact and so is its own derived functor. Its naturality for quotient transitions follows from the same commutative ring maps. The strict coefficient-tower coherence is supplied by [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison].

source.place: Proof, integral-stage paragraph: identify the completed coefficient categories and restriction/direct-image comparisons

proof.text:
Let $I$ denote the strict-tower integral functor of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], with functorial realization fixed by [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. For $K\in D^b_c(Z,R)$, [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] gives a natural isomorphism
$$\psi_K:FK\xrightarrow{\sim}IK=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nF_nK_n.$$
Its $n$-th projection is $F(c_{K,n})$ followed by the coefficient comparison of step 4, coherently on strict towers. By [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible], $IK\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and its actual projection-adjoint reduction maps are isomorphisms. Transport through $\psi_K$ gives $FK\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $(FK)_n\cong F_nK_n$, with those same projection-adjoint maps.
For the triangle comparison, let $\chi_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ be the natural completion map supplied by the identity-extension case of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Use the strict Roos triangle transported through $\chi_K$. Apply the canonical strict-tower comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] and step 4's coherent coefficient comparison. They identify its image under $F$ with the image-tower Roos triangle, including its connecting arrow. The first-object comparison is the canonical $\psi_K$ above: both are the derived comparison of the same composite direct image on the strict reduction tower, precomposed with $F(\chi_K)$. Thus no arbitrary completion of $1-s$ to a triangle is used.

source.place: Proof, integral-stage paragraph: reconstruction, direct-image limits and finite reductions

proof.text:
Fix $P,Q\in D^b_c(Z,R)$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$. The derived change-of-coefficients adjunction [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction], at $Z$ and $X$, gives
$$\Hom_Z(P[m],\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n)\cong\Hom_{Z,A_n}(P_n[m],Q_n),$$
$$\Hom_X(FP[m],\operatorname{Res}_nF_nQ_n)\cong\Hom_{X,A_n}(F_nP_n[m],F_nQ_n).$$
In the second line use the actual reduction isomorphism $(FP)_n\cong F_nP_n$ of step 5. The map on these Hom groups induced by $F$ is precisely $u\mapsto F_nu$ under these adjunctions. Indeed, the transpose of $u:P_n[m]\to Q_n$ is $P[m]\xrightarrow{c_{P,n}}\operatorname{Res}_nP_n[m]\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Res}_nu}\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n$. Applying $F$, and using step 4's coefficient comparison, gives the same formula on $X$ because the reduction comparison of [def-weil-derived-direct-image] is adjoint to the tower projection. Step 5's comparison therefore identifies $F(c_{P,n})$ with $c_{FP,n}$ followed by the reduction comparison. The finite full faithfulness of step 2 now makes the two displayed Hom groups bijective. Naturality in $Q_n$ makes these bijections commute with the quotient transition maps; no assertion that restriction of scalars is fully faithful is being used.

source.place: Proof, integral-stage paragraph: extension/restriction adjunction and compatibility of the Hom bijections

proof.text:
Set $B=\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n$ and $B'=\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_nF_nQ_n$. The product comparison $FB\cong B'$ of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] has $n$-th projection $F$ of the original projection. By the product universal property, for every $m$ the map
$$\Hom_Z(P[m],B)\longrightarrow\Hom_X(FP[m],B')$$
is the product of the bijections in step 6, and hence bijective (the inverse applies their inverses coordinatewise). The transition compatibility in step 6 says it commutes with $1-s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to the Roos triangle of [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] and its rotations, and to the corresponding image triangle supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Writing $A_m=\Hom_Z(P[m],B)$, their five-term exact rows give
$$0\to\operatorname{coker}(1-s:A_1\to A_1)\to\Hom_Z(P,Q)\to\ker(1-s:A_0\to A_0)\to0,$$
and the analogous row on $X$. The maps on both outside terms are isomorphisms by the product bijections. The middle map is $F$ on Hom, because the triangle comparison is the one induced by $F$. For injectivity, a middle element mapping to zero has zero image on the right, hence comes from the left; injectivity on the left then kills it. For surjectivity, lift the right image of a desired middle element through the right isomorphism, lift that to the source middle by exactness, and correct the difference by the left isomorphism. Thus $\Hom_Z(P,Q)\to\Hom_X(FP,FQ)$ is bijective. Naturality of $\psi$ from step 5 gives $I(u)=\psi_QF(u)\psi_P^{-1}$ for the specified integral direct image $I$; conjugation by these isomorphisms is bijective on Hom groups. Together with step 5's codomain check this proves integral full faithfulness for that specified functor.

source.place: Proof, integral-stage paragraph: product terms, Roos triangles and the expanded five-lemma argument

proof.text: At the rational stage use the raw scalar localization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], which has the same objects and $\Hom_E(P,Q)=\Hom_R(P,Q)\otimes_RE$; no Karoubi envelope is present. The integral direct image is $R$-linear: it carries multiplication by a constant scalar to multiplication by the same scalar on sections and on the complexes computing derived direct image and inverse limit. The ambient and full-subcategory scalar action is [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear]. By [def-weil-derived-direct-image], rational direct image is its scalar localization. Therefore its Hom map is the integral Hom bijection of step 7 tensored with $1_E$, with inverse the integral inverse tensored with $1_E$. This proves full faithfulness at $E$ without any flatness inference.

The schemes are Noetherian by step 1 and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The identity completion unit in step 5 and the unit-compatible Koszul/quotient comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] verify ambient derived completeness. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] applies. Steps 3 and 5 verify preservation of the constructible categories; [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies ordinary completed-ring scalar extension with the specified strict-tower extension, including the identity case. After raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], the ambient comparison gives coherent natural isomorphisms
$$\theta_{L/E,P}:F_L(P\otimes_E L)\xrightarrow{\sim}(F_EP)\otimes_E L,$$
where $F_E$ is the specified rational direct image, identified with the ordinary completed direct image by $\psi$. These are the inverses of the comparisons in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].
For $(E,P),(E',Q)$ in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], write $P_L=P\otimes_E L$, $Q_L=Q\otimes_{E'}L$ for each common finite extension $L$. Step 8 gives bijections
$$b_L(u)=\theta_{L/E',Q}F_L(u)\theta_{L/E,P}^{-1}$$
onto the $L$-stage Hom group of the two original direct images. Coherence makes $b_L$ commute with the transition maps. Explicitly, invert a target representative $v$ at stage $L$ by $b_L^{-1}(v)$. If representatives agree at a larger common stage $M$, their inverse images agree there by transition compatibility and injectivity of $b_M$. The rule therefore defines an inverse on the common-stage Hom colimits; both composites are identities already at a representing stage. This proves full faithfulness at $\Qlb$.

source.place: Proof, algebraically closed-stage paragraph; explicit inverse on representatives

proof.text: At a stage with an adjunction $F=i_*\dashv G=Ri^!$, as specified in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], let $\eta$ be its unit. For every $P,Q$ the adjunction sends $F(g)$ to $\eta_Qg$ by naturality of the unit, so full faithfulness just proved implies that $\eta_Q\circ-:\Hom(P,Q)\to\Hom(P,GFQ)$ is bijective. Taking $P=GFQ$ gives $r:GFQ\to Q$ with $\eta_Qr=1$. Taking $P=Q$ and using injectivity gives $r\eta_Q=1$, since postcomposition by $\eta_Q$ sends both $r\eta_Q$ and $1_Q$ to $\eta_Q$. Thus $r$ is a two-sided inverse of the specified adjunction unit $Q\to Ri^!i_*Q$. This spells out the Yoneda argument and needs no new categorical lemma.

source.place: Proof, unit paragraph: the adjunction unit and its explicit inverse

proof.text: Finally, the finite-stage existence clause holds on the entire ordinary ambient derived category: [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support] supplies a right adjoint to termwise $i_*$ for a Noetherian $X$ and a finite constant ring. By step 3 this termwise functor is $Ri_{*,n}$. The finite ambient fully faithful assertion of step 2 and step 10 therefore give the invertible ambient unit for all $Q$, with no boundedness or constructibility assumption. This is exactly the adjunction and unit asserted in [prop-sf-closed-immersion-unit]; its constructible specialization uses the identity compactification in step 1. No existence of a right adjoint at the other coefficient stages is assumed or claimed here beyond the conditional assertion of the item.

source.place: Statement final clause and Proof, unit paragraph: finite ambient right adjoint exists
